clue.text: Habituate to charge reduced by male

indicators.note: reduced tells us the word for charge is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to charge someone is to accuse them
a tom is a male cat, so the word stands for male

explanation.surface: Someone gets used to paying a fee that has been lowered by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To habituate someone is to make them used to something, the same sense as the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Outcry from class over affair

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second, so over sets the order

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: Pupils raise a protest about a scandalous romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest, a noisy uproar.

clue.text: Advantage drug's given to labourer

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug; the 's is just the possessive joining it on
a hand is a manual worker, a labourer

explanation.surface: A worker has been slipped narcotics to give someone an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the advantage over someone means holding control, a position of dominance.

clue.text: Ostentatiously brilliant, yet unusually silent

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the word silent appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something is showy and glittering, yet strangely makes no sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel as an adjective means showy and gaudy, glittering without substance.

clue.text: Easy profit of monopoly — erred breaking it up

indicators.note: breaking it up tells us the preceding words are smashed and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A monopolist went wrong when the business was split up, despite the easy gains.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the three words OF MONOPOLY ERRED, fifteen letters rearranged; 'of' looks like a link word but supplies the O and F.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom for money earned with almost no effort, a soft gain.

clue.text: Bog plant's captivated artist

indicators.note: captivated is read literally as held captive, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: moss is a small flowering-less plant
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter has fallen for some greenery growing in the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a swamp or marshy ground, the same as a bog.

clue.text: Illogical calling lands me in wrong minor suit, initially

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other
wrong signals that the letters of the words before it are put in a mistaken order
initially tells us to take only the opening letter of suit

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a bad call has left them holding the wrong low-ranking suit at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lands' and 'in' only join the pieces; the shuffle of ME and MINOR is followed by S, the first letter of 'suit'. Minor suits in bridge are clubs and diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is a wrong or inappropriate name, so calling something by an illogical label.

clue.text: Fruit bringing Cockney disruption and bother

indicators.note: Cockney speakers are said to drop their H sound, so the first letter goes

parts.note: havoc is chaos or disruption
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Some fruit causes a scene and a fuss in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class dialect of East London, famous for dropping initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped tropical fruit with a large stone.

clue.text: Son unmusical? Altogether useless at audition

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies
someone tone-deaf cannot tell musical notes apart

explanation.surface: A boy with no ear for music is hopeless when trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout for a role, but here it means hearing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely unable to hear is wholly useless at the faculty of hearing.

clue.text: Mother bird gets wet

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A mother swan ends up soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it moist, the verb sense of making wet.

clue.text: Something Joseph achieved, finding rooms not free

indicators.note: free means the letters of the words around it are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what Joseph managed, noting that the rooms were not without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph is Joseph Conrad, the novelist, so his achievement is one of his books; the biblical Joseph is the false trail. 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostromo is a novel published by Joseph Conrad in 1904, one of his works.

clue.text: Bob, in the old days, showing good manners

definitions.meaning: a bob is a quick bend of the knee, and the answer was once an alternative spelling of curtsy
politeness and considerate behaviour towards others

explanation.surface: A curtsy from long ago displays real politeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy means polite behaviour; in older English the same word also named the curtsy.

clue.text: Some hawthorn at Easter is flowery

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Hawthorn in blossom at Easter is full of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'is flowery' is narrowed to 'flowery', since the answer is an adjective and 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowery prose is elaborately decorated, the same as ornate style.

clue.text: I'll be found in long-established secret society

indicators.note: be found in says the letter goes inside the word for long-established

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, meaning long-established
the I of I'll is the letter I, with 'will' completing the instruction

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins an old secretive organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese criminal secret organisation.

clue.text: He takes steps to accentuate the rhythm

definitions.text: He takes steps to accentuate the rhythm

parts.words: He takes steps to accentuate the rhythm
parts.note: sounds like a conductor or drummer, but the steps are literal dance steps that beat out the rhythm with metal-tipped shoes

explanation.definitionFit: This performer dances with metal-plated shoes whose steps sound out the beat.

clue.text: One keeps to the bed mostly, taking port by oneself

definitions.text: One keeps to the bed mostly

parts.note: Dover is the Kent port on the English Channel
sole means alone, by oneself

explanation.surface: Someone stays in bed most of the time, drinking port alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the sea bed, not a bed for sleeping, and 'port' is the town, not the wine. DOVER is a ferry port in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish lives on the sea floor, spending most of its time on the seabed.

clue.text: It may get us nearest being drunk

definitions.text: It may get us nearest being drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink that brings us closest to intoxication.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a sweet French wine is something that may make us drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white Bordeaux wine, the sort of drink that can make you tipsy.

clue.text: See flower sheltered from this wind

indicators.note: sheltered means one piece is protected inside the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Look at a blossom protected from the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts as a river, but here it is the bloom. A see is the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Celtic chief found prison to be boring

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, informally a prison
to drag on is to go on tediously, to be boring

explanation.surface: A tribal leader finds jail tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendragon was a title of ancient British rulers, as with Uther, father of Arthur.

clue.text: Candidate getting no marks in English, repeatedly

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter for English is written twice

explanation.surface: An applicant scores zero in an English exam, time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for election or an award, a candidate.

clue.text: Lower in volume, as being very loud

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as being
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Turn it down, since it's far too noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower in volume' looks like turning the sound down; it means downing a drink in large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaff is to drink heartily, knocking back a large quantity, as you lower a pint.

clue.text: Manipulate in rage

definitions.meaning: to shape or mould something with the hands
a rage is a craze, the latest trend, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: Someone handles things while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: in fashion is in the rage, so the two senses are joined by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion is to form or mould, and a fashion is a current craze.

clue.text: Spot's bark

definitions.meaning: a spot is a tight corner or fix; the 's stands for 'is', joining the two senses
to bark a shin is to graze the skin off it

explanation.surface: A dog named Spot gives a woof.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot reads as a dog's name and bark as its noise; in fact a spot is a predicament and to bark is to graze.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, and to scrape skin is to graze it.

clue.text: Virtually nothing received by charity by end of Lent

indicators.note: received by means the first piece is taken inside the second

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of Lent

explanation.surface: Charity gets almost nothing as Lent closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtually means nearly, all but completely.

clue.text: Way to prepare potatoes and game in appropriate container

indicators.note: in says the game sits inside the word for appropriate, which acts as the container

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate, as in due respect
chess is the board game

explanation.surface: A recipe for potatoes and meat served in a suitable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like meat for the pot beside the potatoes, but it is the board game; 'container' simply confirms which piece holds the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are mashed with egg, piped and baked, a classic preparation.

clue.text: Arrange old musical item

parts.note: to concert something is to arrange it by agreement

explanation.surface: Someone sets up an old piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical composition for a solo instrument and orchestra.

clue.text: An epic narration, explaining Italian developments originally

definitions.text: An epic narration, explaining Italian developments originally

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of each word in the clue

explanation.surface: A long poem tells the story of how Italy came about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Virgil's epic recounts Aeneas's voyage to Italy, the founding story of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeneid is Virgil's Latin epic poem telling of Aeneas, ancestor of the Romans.

clue.text: Cold and damp, but spacious for audience?

indicators.note: for audience says we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: roomy means having plenty of space

explanation.surface: A place is chilly and wet but big enough to hold a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumy describes air that is raw and damp, likely to bring on a chill.

clue.text: Archdeacon's gone shakily round for service

indicators.note: round says the shaken letters go around the archdeacon's piece
shakily means the letters of gone tremble into a new order

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's gone wobbly around the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakily' rearranges the four letters of 'gone' to EONG, and 'round' wraps those letters about the archdeacon's title plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Church of England.
